newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-BEATEN NARDIELLO FOUGHT WITH BROKEN HAND.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-BEATEN NARDIELLO FOUGHT WITH BROKEN HAND.

text.p: Italy's Vincenzo Nardiello, who lost his World Boxing Council (WBC) super-middleweight title to Briton Robin Reid on Saturday, said on Sunday he had fought with a broken bone in his hand.
"This was bad luck. Fighting in these circumstances was impossible," said Nardiello, his left arm in plaster. American referee Frank Cappuccino stopped the fight in the seventh round.
"I broke my hand in the first round, I tried an uppercut and hit Reid on the head.
"I felt bad, I told my manager but he didn't believe me...so I gritted my teeth for six rounds," the Italian added.
"If it had happened in the seventh, maybe a few points ahead, it would have been different."

Nardiello, who was whistled by fans who thought he was seeking sanctuary in protesting low blows and complaining about his opponent rather than taking him on, said he wanted his revenge on Reid and was willing to fight in England.
"I'm not finished. Maybe this is just the launch pad. I have shown that I know how to keep fighting. I don't know how many others would have been able to in my place," he said.

The unbeaten Reid, nicknamed "The Grim Reaper", was recognised to have deserved his win by disappointed Italian fans usually totally behind their man. It was Nardiello's first defence since he won the title in July.
